---
title: "Defining Treatment: Yelp Review Surges"
author: "Manos Giannitselis"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r example-data, echo=FALSE}
# Small simulated stand-in for the real county-year panel (agg_trim_pca),
# so this file runs standalone. See README for context.
set.seed(42)
n_counties <- 30
years <- 2015:2023

df <- expand.grid(
  county_name = paste0("County_", 1:n_counties),
  year        = years
) %>%
  arrange(county_name, year) %>%
  group_by(county_name) %>%
  mutate(
    # simulate a review "takeoff" at a random year for some counties
    takeoff_year   = sample(c(2017:2021, rep(NA, 10)), 1),
    avg_log_reviews = ifelse(
      !is.na(takeoff_year) & year >= takeoff_year,
      rnorm(n(), 3, 0.5),
      rnorm(n(), 1, 0.3)
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Binary treatment: percentile threshold

```{r binary-treatment}
# A county-year is "high review activity" if avg_log_reviews exceeds the
# 75th percentile of the full sample that year-over-year.
thr75 <- quantile(df$avg_log_reviews, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)

first_treat <- df %>%
  group_by(county_name) %>%
  summarise(first_year = min(year[avg_log_reviews > thr75], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

did_df <- df %>%
  left_join(first_treat, by = "county_name") %>%
  mutate(
    treated   = as.integer(!is.na(first_year)),
    post      = as.integer(year >= first_year),
    did_bin   = treated * post   # binary DiD interaction term
  )

table(did_df$treated)
head(did_df %>% select(county_name, year, avg_log_reviews, first_year, treated, post, did_bin), 10)
```

```{r binary-treatment-plot}
did_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(first_year)) %>%
  distinct(county_name, first_year) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = first_year)) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Timing of First Treatment (Yelp Surge)",
    x = "Year", y = "Number of Counties"
  )
```

## Continuous treatment: review intensity

```{r continuous-treatment}
# Instead of collapsing review activity into 0/1, use the raw intensity
# (log reviews) directly, interacted with the post-treatment window.
did_df <- did_df %>%
  mutate(
    intensity = avg_log_reviews,
    did_cont  = intensity * post
  )

head(did_df %>% select(county_name, year, intensity, post, did_cont), 10)
```

## Alternative thresholds

```{r alt-thresholds}
# Rather than committing to one arbitrary cutoff, multiple percentile
# thresholds are tried (60th, 75th, 90th) to see how the binary
# treatment definition behaves as the bar for "high review activity"
# is raised or lowered. This was also a step toward thinking about
# treatment as a matter of degree (dosage) rather than yes/no -- which
# is what the continuous specification above captures more directly.
thr60 <- quantile(df$avg_log_reviews, 0.60, na.rm = TRUE)
thr90 <- quantile(df$avg_log_reviews, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)

c(thr60 = thr60, thr75 = thr75, thr90 = thr90)
```
